doc.title: Howard Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2025

title: First concerto rehearsal, new concerto and Harry Shearer
summary: Levy recalls being moved hearing his first concerto, describes the new odd-meter concerto, and mentions playing gigs with Harry Shearer.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: It makes me think of – can you recall the first time, with your first concerto, that first rehearsal and how you felt when you heard it. Did it sound – were you surprised?

Yeah I was going to say you know I wrote with pencil. I didn’t have midi, or I wasn’t using Finale, it was just all in my head. I just wrote at the piano and on the harmonica and at my kitchen table and hotel rooms. So yeah, I was surprised and actually, there were certain parts of the piece that actually moved me emotionally and I kind of got choked up. It was like, “Okay Howard, come on man, you know, you can’t be moved by your own music, you have to concentrate here and play.” But that was the biggest surprise was being moved by what I had written, that it really affected me emotionally. Yeah. So this new one, I don't know what’s going to happen. Because it’s almost all in odd time meters. It’s inspired by Bulgarian and Macedonian, Romanian and Greek music. There’s a lot of things in five and seven and nine and eleven. I didn’t go any higher than eleven. Like Spinal Tap you know?
I just read a book about Spinal Tap.
Oh Harry Shearer is a friend of mine.

We played a bunch of gigs together. He’s a very good musician. He writes really interesting tunes, like with very unstandard changes in them. It’s like whoa. Very interesting guy and a huge music head. I mean just – I think I’m going to see him in New Orleans when the Flecktones play our last show.
